sections.h2: Why is Oak Ridge a distinct place to sell a house?
sections.html:
Oak Ridge was built in 1942 as a Manhattan Project site, and it was incorporated as a city in 1959. The federal government bought nearly 60,000 acres of farmland in the Clinch River valley and laid out a planned town about 25 miles east of Knoxville. Many of the first houses were put up fast from cemesto panels, which are bonded cement and asbestos, so an inspector or buyer may ask about the original construction of an older house here.

The city sits across five parallel ridges and four valleys, with Melton Hill Lake on its northeast and east edges. Census figures give the city 85.25 square miles of land and 35,395 residents for mid-2025, a 12.7% climb since the 2020 base. Oak Ridge National Laboratory and the Y-12 complex remain major employers, and the school district's own news release mentions growth in the nuclear industry as a reason to plan for more students.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show about Oak Ridge homes?
sections.html:
QuickFacts lists a $270,200 median value for houses their owners live in (2020 to 2024), and 65.8% of homes fit that description. Renters pay a median $1,131. The 14,015 households average 2.30 people, and people 65 and over make up 19.6% of the city against 18.9% nationwide.

  • Median household income: $72,311
  • Adults 25 and older holding a four-year degree: 40.2%
  • Typical trip to work: 21.7 minutes
  • Residents in poverty: 12.2%

With so many older residents, a good share of listings come from downsizing or estate sales. See Census QuickFacts for Oak Ridge for the full list.

sections.h2: Does Oak Ridge send one tax bill or two?
sections.html:
Two. The city mails its own statement in July and collects it through the Utilities Business Office at 200 South Tulane Avenue, while the county portion is billed by Anderson or Roane County depending on where the parcel lies. About 16.25% of taxable real parcels are in the Roane County section. The city's published rate table shows the following.

Section of Oak RidgeCity rateCounty rateTotal per $100
Anderson County (tax year 2023)$2.3136$2.456$4.7696
Roane County (tax year 2022)$2.3136$2.34$4.6536

Houses are assessed at a quarter of appraised value. For the $270,200 median that means $67,550 on the roll, and the city share at $2.3136 comes to roughly $1,563. The table stops at those years, so call the Utilities Business Office at (865) 425-3400 for the current figure. Source: the city's tax rate page.

sections.h2: When is Oak Ridge city tax due?
sections.html:
The city allows payment without interest until August 31; accrual begins September 1. Pay online, at the Utilities Business Office, in the lot drop box, or send a check to P.O. Box 1, Oak Ridge, TN 37831. The city passes on a 2.75% fee for card payments, and eChecks cost $1 for each $5,000.

Statements go to whatever owner address the state held on January 1. After a spring or summer sale, the new owner may never receive one, and the city says closing normally covers that gap. A missing notice never erases the debt. The city bill falls due in summer and the county bill in the fall, so a seller closing between the two should have the title company pull both.

sections.h2: How recent is the last reappraisal for Oak Ridge properties?
sections.html:
The city reports that properties in both the Anderson and Roane sections were reappraised in fiscal years 2016 and 2021, tied to tax years 2015 and 2020. The city rate fell from $2.56 in the 2019 tax year to $2.3136 after that second reappraisal, a drop of about 10%, while the Anderson County rate fell from $2.6945 to $2.456.

Assessment ratios are fixed by state law at 25% for residential property, 40% for commercial and 30% for personal equipment. The city does not set appraised values, so an owner who disagrees with one should ask the Anderson or Roane County assessor how to request a review.

sections.h2: What property tax relief exists for Oak Ridge owners?
sections.html:
Tennessee's freeze and relief programs run through the counties. The Comptroller's 2026 list puts the freeze income ceiling at $53,900 in Anderson County and $43,460 in Roane County, and applications close 35 days after the local delinquency date.

A seller who already benefits from one should say so before closing, so the settlement figures track the bill that is really owed.

sections.h2: What local rules affect an Oak Ridge house sale?
sections.html:
Call Codes Enforcement at 865-425-3532 for building permits; the division also polices housing, plumbing, electrical and zoning rules. Permit work now runs through the CityView portal. The city also publishes a three-day appeal form for housing code violations, and it must be returned in person within three days of signing for a certified notice.

  • A vacant building must keep its doors and windows locked or otherwise secured.
  • Every house must show its number at the front entrance or on the mailbox.
  • A structure tax-delinquent for three years can be treated as deteriorated under the rental inspection chapter.

Chapter 5 of Title 13 allows residential rental inspection districts, so a landlord with a rental to sell should ask Planning and Development whether the address is in one. See the city's Codes Enforcement page.

sections.h2: How does the recording process work for Oak Ridge sales?
sections.html:
A deed goes on record in the county where the land lies. For Anderson County that is the Register of Deeds in Clinton, 100 North Main Street, Room 205 (weekdays, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.), which puts its indexes online free of user fees. The state adds a 37-cent levy per $100 of sale price.

Check which county holds your parcel before ordering a title search, because Anderson and Roane keep separate records and tax maps. Most sellers leave the search and filing to the title company.

sections.h2: How are Oak Ridge schools and neighborhoods likely to figure in buyer questions?
sections.html:
Oak Ridge Schools counted 4,853 students in 2024 to 2025, ended the following year at 4,694, and had 4,795 enrolled by August 2026. The city has its own district, so out-of-town buyers may ask about zoning for a given address; the district can confirm.

Many homes sit on the steep northeastern slope of Blackoak Ridge, and the east-side lakefront has trails and picnic areas, so lot shape and slope matter more here than in a flat grid. Climate adds detail: the area averages about 59.7 inches of rain a year and 39 days at or above 90 degrees, so gutters, drainage and air conditioning are routine inspection items.

sections.h2: What are the fastest ways to sell an Oak Ridge house?
sections.html:
An agent listing works for a tidy house whose owner can wait on a buyer's loan. Cash offers tend to suit houses that need work, inherited houses and rentals with tenants, and closing then depends on clear title and lien payoffs.

Whatever the buyer, put the offer in writing, settle who covers recording tax, and let the title company verify the city and county tax status.

faqs.q: When does Oak Ridge city property tax become delinquent?
faqs.a: Interest starts September 1. Statements arrive in July, and August 31 is the last day to pay without it.

faqs.q: Which county handles my Oak Ridge deed?
faqs.a: Whichever county holds the parcel. Anderson holds most of the city, and about 16.25% of taxable real parcels sit in Roane County, so check your tax map first.

faqs.q: What is the Oak Ridge city tax rate?
faqs.a: $2.3136 per $100 assessed in the city's table through its last listed year. The Utilities Business Office, (865) 425-3400, can tell you the rate on this year's bill.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to repair a house before selling it in Oak Ridge?
faqs.a: For building work, yes. Codes Enforcement issues every building permit, and trade permits go to applicants with valid city or state licenses. The number is 865-425-3532.

faqs.q: Can a buyer see my county records online?
faqs.a: Yes for Anderson County. Its Register of Deeds offers online access to indexes and images and has removed user fees.
